title: a-device-reaches-trouble-over-the-bus-never-by-import
from_idea: none, because the origin is a deterministic build_inspector finding, not a captured idea: device_isolation_holds at devices/cairn and devices/web_server, live in the trouble store as inspector-new-finding-device-isolation-holds-devices-cairn and -devices-web-server (`cairn operator show inbox`), raised by the sieve at cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py (ruling 3f4887e, 2026-09-01) against imports added 2026-09-04 (1844ef6)
intention: The cairn device and web_server reach the trouble device over the bus, and cairn's trouble-panel probe reaches web_server's renderer the same way, so no device imports another device (db_domain stays the sole exception) and the isolation sieve reads green with the panel still live.
why: The trouble panel Akien opens shows live troubles because cairn/device.py and web_server/listener.py instantiate TroubleDevice directly — the panel works, and the isolation sieve reds both devices on every inspector run (2 live troubles, 3 findings, since the panel landed 2026-09-04). The lived symptom is a permanent red on the dashboard that nobody can clear without the code moving.
how: trouble answers three verbs on the bus — `live` (JSON list), `raise <identity> --why ...`, `clear <identity> --by ... --what-changed ...` — through the same shim contract inference_domain answers `infer` with (cairn/devices/codemother/watch.py:45 is the client pattern: connect_bus().request(device, verbs, ...)). cairn/device.py's _trouble_pane_data and web_server/listener.py's _handle_ws_troubles become bus requests for `live`. The probe cairn/devices/cairn/probes/trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles.py stops importing web_server.render: it asks web_server's `render` verb for the pane, or berths beside web_server if what it measures is web_server's rendering. build_inspector's own import of TroubleDevice is a machine, not a device, and is outside this ticket.
falsifier: DONE when (1) `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector` reports zero device_isolation_holds findings at devices/cairn and devices/web_server; (2) `grep -rn 'cairn.devices.trouble' cairn/devices --include=*.py` matches only under cairn/devices/trouble/; (3) the probe trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles still proves green with a raised fixture trouble visible in the rendered pane; (4) the two inspector troubles are cleared by reconcile, not by hand. WRONG INTENT if the bus round trip makes the panel's WebSocket push miss its 1s budget — then the fix is a subscription, not a request.
traces_to: Law 6 — everything has exactly one owner and the owner alone gates writes: trouble's store is trouble's, and a direct TroubleDevice() from another device's process writes it ambiently. Ruling no-cross-device-imports (memory RULED; sieve 3f4887e): only db_domain may be imported across devices. Encapsulation is the complexity budget: each device stays inside CC's limit through the standard bus contract.
watchme: none, because the signal is a deterministic sieve (device_isolation_holds in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py) that already runs on every inspector pass and at-rest on the beat — it IS the watch, and a regression re-raises inspector-new-finding-device-isolation-holds-* in the trouble store
owner: cairn device (devices/cairn) owns the pane and the probe; web_server owns its listener; trouble owns the verbs it answers. CC builds; codemother reviews the crossing.
author: CC
